title: Moldova to host the Balkan Senior Table Tennis Championships for the first time in 2027
excerpt: The Republic of Moldova will host the Balkan Senior Table Tennis Championships for the first time, from 23 to 28 August 2027.
body_html:
The Republic of Moldova is preparing to host, for the first time, the Balkan Senior Table Tennis Championships, scheduled for 23-28 August 2027. Organising the competition is an important moment for Moldovan table tennis and a chance to raise our country's profile on the regional sports stage.

The event will bring together athletes, coaches and representatives of the national federations of the Balkan region, giving the Republic of Moldova the opportunity to show its capacity to organise international competitions and to strengthen its cooperation with sports partners in the region.

As part of the preparations for the championships, Milorad TRPKOVSKI, General Secretary of the Balkan Table Tennis Union (BTTU), made a working visit to the Republic of Moldova, during which he examined the sports infrastructure and the conditions planned for the competition.

The programme of the visit also included a meeting with Maxim POTÎRNICHE, member of the Parliament of the Republic of Moldova, attended by representatives of the Table Tennis Federation of the Republic of Moldova. The talks focused on the prospects of organising the championships, the importance of institutional support for sport and the opportunities to develop table tennis nationally.

Another significant result for Moldova's representation in international sports bodies is the election of Oleg ȘARIC, President of the Table Tennis Federation of the Republic of Moldova, as President of the Balkan Table Tennis Union (BTTU) for a one-year term. The decision, adopted at the BTTU Congress, reflects the growing role of the Moldovan Federation in regional sports cooperation and opens new prospects for promoting table tennis in our country.

The National Sports Association ATTP supports the organisation of the 2027 Balkan Championships and reaffirms its readiness to help, together with the Table Tennis Federation of the Republic of Moldova, prepare and run this international event. Through its experience in organising competitions, developing sports infrastructure and promoting table tennis, ATTP aims to support the joint effort to hold the championships to high organisational and sporting standards.

Hosting the Balkan Championships is also an opportunity to bring table tennis to a wider public, to spark young people's interest in the sport and to make the most of the Republic of Moldova's organisational potential.

For ATTP, this competition is a new opportunity to contribute to the development of Moldovan table tennis and to the sporting prestige of the Republic of Moldova internationally.
